title: Tiroler Steinöl Vitalberg Pertisau
name: Tiroler Steinöl Vitalberg Pertisau
kurzbeschreibung: The Tiroler Steinöl Vitalberg in Pertisau on Lake Achensee: glass museum celebrating the "black gold of the Alps", Bächelsberg tunnel, and panorama café.
beschreibung:
Overview

The architecturally distinctive Tiroler Steinöl Vitalberg is located in the picturesque alpine village of Pertisau on the southwestern shore of Lake Achensee at an altitude of around 940 metres. Nestled between the gentle shores of Tyrol's largest lake and the rugged limestone crags of the Karwendel Nature Park, this modern glass museum building presents the unique cultural and extraction history of world-famous Tyrolean shale oil. As a healing natural remedy derived from fossilised marine sediments of the Karwendel mountains, this "black gold of the Alps" has been prized for over a century for its soothing and therapeutic qualities.

History & Shale Oil Extraction

The discovery of this precious resource dates back to 1902, when local pioneer Martin Albrecht discovered oil-bearing oil shale in the Bächental in the Karwendel mountains. From the fossil-rich rock – remnants of a tropical prehistoric sea dating back more than 180 million years – he distilled, through painstaking manual work, mineral- and sulphur-rich shale oil, which quickly gained fame as a highly effective household remedy for rheumatic aches, muscle tension, and skin conditions. To this day, the founding Albrecht family mines the oil shale underground at an altitude of 1,500 metres on the Bächelsberg. The Vitalberg museum illustrates this fascinating process: inside an authentically reconstructed mining gallery, visitors experience the arduous labour of the shale miners, historical distillation retorts, and the geological creation of the Alps. The visitor experience is crowned by the glass-fronted Panorama-Café on the upper floor, affording sweeping views across the emerald-green waters of the Achensee.

Visit & Getting There

The Tiroler Steinöl Vitalberg visitor centre is open year-round: from May to October daily from 09:00 to 18:00, and during the winter months from November to April daily from 10:00 to 17:00. Museum admission prices (2025/2026 season): adults approx. €6.50, reduced and seniors approx. €5.50, children (6 to 15 years) approx. €3.50; children under 6 years free. Admission is free with the regional Achensee Erlebniscard. Getting there by public transport: take ÖBB trains to Jenbach railway station, and from there either take the historic Achenseebahn (steam cog railway) or VVT bus route 4080 directly to Pertisau (stops Pertisau Karwendellift or Pertisau Information, just a three-minute walk away). By car: via the Inntalautobahn A12, exit Wiesing/Achensee, follow the B181 to Maurach and continue to Pertisau (parking available directly at the building or at the Karwendel cable car station).

Tips

The entire Vitalberg museum, the shop, and the panorama café are barrier-free and fully accessible with a modern passenger lift; accessible toilets are also provided. In the on-site Steinöl-Shop, you can sample the authentic skincare and healing products directly. Combine your visit with a scenic boat cruise on Lake Achensee or an excursion into the idyllic Karwendel valleys (Falzthurntal and Gerntal).
